title: Choose the visual world
question: Choose the visual system that should govern the shell and framework surfaces.

options.label: The Executive Docket
options.lineage: legal dockets, audit registers, and executive review folios
options.thesis: Every project becomes a precise living case file with evidence, decisions, and status held in one calm hierarchy.
options.viewport: A black navigation spine frames a warm off-white working sheet with compact project context, a dense record table, and a narrow evidence rail.
options.risk: It can feel conservative if motion, depth, and active states are too restrained.

raised.raise: Dependencies and workflow pressure become traceable instead of merely listed.
Surface levels gain a disciplined light-to-dark depth scale.
State changes use crisp illumination and a short, elegant afterglow.
Critical status receives decisive scale without permanent visual alarm.
Transitions reveal committed state changes with deliberate timing.
Dense regions keep every object clearly named and locally understandable.

options.label: The Corporate Editorial
options.lineage: modern annual reports, financial editorial systems, and precision product interfaces
options.thesis: Operational density is composed like a first-rate business publication: confident type, generous alignment, and exact information rhythm.
options.viewport: A compact black rail and floating off-white workspace use a strong page title, quiet metadata, and publication-grade table hierarchy.
options.risk: This is the most familiar modern-corporate direction and can resemble premium SaaS products if the details are timid.

options.label: The Tension Network
options.lineage: tensegrity structures and engineering force diagrams
options.thesis: Quality and safety work appears as a network of accountable forces, where every issue connects to its owner, countermeasure, and consequence.
options.viewport: A precise black shell opens onto a dense work surface whose status rail and dependency lines expose where projects are balanced or under strain.
options.case: It gives workflow dependencies unusual clarity, but its structural metaphor is less familiar to office administrators.
options.risk: Visible connection lines can become decoration when a screen has few real dependencies.

options.label: The Depth Profile
options.thesis: Workflow depth controls light, focus, and urgency.
options.viewport: A vertical status axis descends through project risk and evidence.
options.case: It makes depth vivid but makes ordinary administration feel theatrical.
options.kept: A rigorous luminance scale for semantic surface depth.
options.risk: The ocean metaphor can overpower routine work.

options.label: The Crisis Wall
options.thesis: Critical conditions become impossible to miss on absolute black.
options.viewport: Dense framed readings surround one monumental condition state.
options.case: It is clear during emergencies but too playful and alarm-heavy for routine administration.
options.kept: Critical conditions may briefly claim decisive visual scale.
options.risk: It turns normal work into a permanent emergency.

options.label: The Labeled Cutaway
options.thesis: Every active part stays visible and clearly named.
options.viewport: A continuous project scene exposes each workflow in place.
options.case: Its labeling discipline helps density, but its illustration language directly conflicts with the non-playful brief.
options.kept: Dense regions must remain locally legible and clearly labeled.
options.risk: It is inherently playful and decorative.

options.label: The Struck State
options.thesis: Current state strikes forward from quiet historical ghosts.
options.viewport: Unframed black planes hold selected values as crisp warm light over faint history.
options.case: Its state grammar is elegant, but ghosted alternatives reduce clarity in dense forms and tables.
options.kept: Selected states strike crisply and old states decay over one short beat.
options.risk: The display effect can reduce readability.

options.label: The Deliberate Reveal
options.thesis: Committed workflow changes reveal themselves with deliberate timing.
options.viewport: Ordered workflow stations move from quiet preview to committed result.
options.case: It supports careful workflows but imposes a sequential process on screens that also need free navigation.
options.kept: Committed transitions use deliberate reveal timing.
options.risk: Amber light can make the whole product feel themed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished enterprise SaaS shell with a neutral sidebar, white cards, and a conventional blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar fixed sidebar, top bar, summary cards, and data table.
canonCard.risk: It is clear but intentionally indistinguishable from other enterprise software.
